newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican bellwether Cetes rate rises on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Mexican bellwether Cetes rate rises on uncertainty.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate rose slightly at the Banco de Mexico's primary treasury bill auction on Tuesday, but rates fell in the longer terms as investors locked in high real rates, analysts said.

Analysts said the slight increase in the one-month paper was due to uncertainty before the next meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on November 13, and before the Mexican government outlines its economic objectives for 1997 on Thursday.
"The 28-day paper covers events like the government's presentation and the meeting of the Fed, which could cause some pressures, so the increase was mainly due to speculation," said one analyst.
Strong demand for the longer-term paper helped push down those rates. Analysts have been recommending Mexican longer-term Cetes recently.

Earlier Tuesday, for example, ING Barings recommended six-month treasury bills in a report, saying the peso was unlikely to depreciate rapidly. It said the six-month Cetes could give an annualized return of about 13 percent in dollar terms.
Limited room for peso depreciation gives the opportunity for a healthy real return with a small risk, analysts said.
On Tuesday, the Mexican peso reversed early gains to close weaker against the dollar. The benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.95 centavos weaker at 7.9125/7.9175 per dollar.
But the peso has been stronger since weakening through 8.0 pesos to the dollar recently. The peso weakened due to political and economic concerns.
At the primary auction on Tuesday, the 28-day Cetes rate rose 11 basis points to 29.45 percent, while the 91-day rate fell 120 basis points to 28.90 percent.
The 182-day rate fell 161 basis points to 27.69 percent.
The one-year paper was assigned at 27.15 percent this week, compared with 28.63 percent last week.
The rate on the bellwether 28-day Cetes rose to 29.34 percent last week, the third increase in a row. It was as low as 22.74 percent in early October.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders on Tuesday had shown an average forecast of 29.13 percent for the 28-day Cetes rate, a fall of 21 basis points from last week's auction.
